title: Linzer cookies
summary: Hazelnut-almond sandwich cookies with a window of quick raspberry chia jam, dusted with powdered sweetener.
steps: For the jam, simmer the raspberries, erythritol and lemon juice for 5 minutes, mashing the fruit. Stir in the chia seeds and cool; it thickens as it stands.
Beat the butter and ⅓ cup powdered erythritol until smooth, then beat in the egg yolk, lemon zest and vanilla. Stir in the hazelnut flour, almond flour, cinnamon and salt.
Divide the dough in two, flatten into discs, wrap and chill 1 hour.
Heat the oven to 165 °C (325 °F) and line two baking sheets with parchment.
Roll each disc between parchment to 3 mm (⅛ in) thick and cut 28 rounds with a 6 cm (2½ in) cutter. Cut a small window from the centre of half of them. Re-chill if the dough softens.
Bake 10–12 minutes, until the edges just colour. Cool completely on the sheets.
Dust the window cookies with powdered erythritol. Spread about 1 teaspoon of jam on each solid cookie and top with a window cookie.
dairy_free_notes: The dairy-free dough is softer and tears more easily; roll it straight from the fridge and chill the cut rounds for 10 minutes before baking.
tips: Assemble on the day you serve them; the jam softens the cookies overnight.

origin.history: The Linzer torte, a nut pastry filled with jam under a lattice, is named after the Austrian city of Linz and is among the oldest named cakes in Europe; a recipe for it survives from the seventeenth century. The sandwich cookies with a jam window are a later, smaller version of the same pastry, and are now a Christmas staple in Austria and beyond.
